introduction.heading: Plumbing for Sandy homes
introduction.body:
Half of the homes in Sandy were built in 1985 or later, and about 42% before 1980, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. Many of those homes are reaching the age when water heaters, faucets and fixtures need replacing. A water heater usually lasts 10 to 15 years.

Sandy City Public Utilities supplies water from Little Cottonwood Creek, Bell Canyon Creek and the Ontario Drain Tunnel, plus stored water from Deer Creek and Jordanelle reservoirs delivered by the Metropolitan Water District of Salt Lake & Sandy. Sixteen city wells add groundwater, mostly in summer.

Because Sandy's wells usually run only in summer to meet peak demand, the mix of water in the pipes changes through the year.
